TradingAgents: Towards Agentic Finance Research

Quick start

1. Get an API key

  • Sign up at Tauric Research.
  • Create your Tauric API key.

2. Install

curl -fsSL https://tauric.ai/tradingagents/install.sh | sh

Or with npm: npm i -g @tauric/tradingagents

3. Run

tradingagents

Start your agentic finance research with Tauric!

Models

Provider Needs
Tauric AI Tauric API key
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, OpenRouter their API key
Self-hosted models (vLLM, Ollama) its address and model
AI subscriptions (ChatGPT) tradingagents login chatgpt

With another provider, /login adds a Tauric API key for filings, statements and news. See docs/models.md.

Usage

Type a question and press Enter. Every figure in the answer is marked with its source, and a numbered list of sources follows.

Command Does
/ Open the commands
/model Choose the model and how hard it reasons
/resume Resume an earlier session
/export Save the last answer as a PDF report, or the session as Markdown
/copy Copy the last answer
/help List every command and key

Shift+Tab switches to plan mode, where the agent proposes a research plan first.

Architecture

Agents and skills

The main agent plans the research, reads what the question needs with its data tools, and works the numbers with its compute tools. For depth, it briefs specialist agents, each in its own context:

Agent Covers
Equity Research a company's statements, filings, estimates, valuation, ownership and news
Macro Strategy growth, inflation, rates and the yield curve, credit, sectors, cross-asset moves
Quant Research returns, volatility, drawdowns, correlation and beta, technical indicators
Risk Analysis what could make a position lose, and what would show it early

For a known kind of research it follows a skill:

Area Skills
Companies company snapshot, earnings preview and review, filing review, full analysis
Valuation DCF, relative valuation, scenario analysis
Markets macro outlook, market brief, performance comparison, sector review, technical analysis
Risk portfolio review, risk assessment, thesis review

You can add your own agents and skills as Markdown files (docs/usage.md). TradingAgents researches and answers; it does not place trades.

Documentation

  • Install: the installer, npm, release files and updates.
  • Usage: the terminal, one-off questions, sessions, agents and skills, sources, sync and limits.
  • Models: providers, keys, reasoning and OpenAI-compatible servers.
  • Configuration: files and environment variables.

To report an issue or open a pull request, see CONTRIBUTING.md; to report a security problem, SECURITY.md.

Citation

@article{xiao2024tradingagents,
  title={TradingAgents: Multi-agents LLM financial trading framework},
  author={Xiao, Yijia and Sun, Edward and Luo, Di and Wang, Wei},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2412.20138},
  year={2024}
}

License

Apache-2.0. See LICENSE.

releases.name: v1.0.1
releases.body:
### Fixed

- Plan mode: the PDF report shows the question you asked, with what you added while planning, instead of "Carry out the plan".
- Reports: the report starts with the answer; progress notes written along the way are left out.
- Price history: a one-year window that spans February 29 is no longer refused.
- Correlation: returns over only three shared dates are refused instead of reported as a perfect +1 or -1; four dates are the minimum.
- API keys: saving a key confirms it by the provider's name ("Stored the Tauric API key").

### Added

- Price history: two-, three- and five-year windows in one request.

### Updated

- Runtime: Bun 1.4.5, with its security fixes.

releases.name: v1.0.0
releases.body:
- TradingAgents: Towards Agentic Finance Research.

### Research

- Agents: Equity Research, Macro Strategy, Quant Research and Risk Analysis research in parallel and report back.
- Skills: sixteen built-in research methods, from an earnings review to a DCF valuation.
- Your own agents and skills, as Markdown files.
- Plan mode: review and revise a research plan before it runs.
- Sources: every figure is cited to the data it came from.

### Data and models

- Data: with a Tauric API key, market data, fundamentals, filings, news, economic series and prediction-market odds.
- Compute: statistics, risk, technical indicators, valuation and portfolio construction over the data read.
- Models: Tauric AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, AI subscriptions (ChatGPT), or self-hosted models.

### Sessions and output

- Sessions: resume any session, and sync sessions to your Tauric account.
- Export: a PDF report or Markdown; `/copy` copies the answer.
- Scripting: `tradingagents -p` answers one question; `--json` streams events; `--limit` caps time, tokens and steps.

### Install

- `curl -fsSL https://tauric.ai/tradingagents/install.sh | sh` or `npm i

releases.name: TradingAgents v0.7.1
releases.body:
Decisions are scored only on final closes and settle across long market holidays, a model's unpadded date no longer reads filings made after the run date, and fixes to portfolios, prices, SEC statements, reports, Azure and Claude settings.

## Upgrading from 0.7.0

- Docker images no longer include `.env.enterprise`. For Azure OpenAI in Docker, put its keys in `.env`.

## Fixed

- A date a model passes without zero padding, such as `2024-7-5`, is read as that date. It could compare as later than a filing made after the run date, and SEC EDGAR then served that filing. (#1488)
- A decision is no longer scored on the bar of a session still trading, and one made before a market closure longer than a week, such as a national holiday, settles once trading resumes instead of staying pending. (#1548, #1539)
- A backtest reports the failures of its last settlement pass, and two started in the same second no longer share one run. (#1557, #1549)
- A holding listed under a broker's spelling (`BTCUSDT`, `700.HK`) is matched to the instrument analyzed, and a portfolio number that is not finite is refused when the file loads. (#1556, #1509)
- Prices keep their significant digits: a sub-cent close

releases.name: TradingAgents v0.7.0
releases.body:
Runs on your ChatGPT plan, backtests scored from the first close after each decision, a note at start-up when a newer release is out, and a wheel attached to each GitHub release.

## Added

- **Your ChatGPT plan.** The `chatgpt` provider runs TradingAgents on a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan instead of an API key, through OpenAI's sign-in for open-source apps. Choose "Subscription" in the CLI's provider menu; for unattended runs, Docker and Python (`llm_provider="chatgpt"`), sign in once with `tradingagents login chatgpt`. `tradingagents logout chatgpt` revokes the sign-in. The CLI lists the plan's models, and reasoning effort applies as it does for OpenAI. (#1194, #1475)
- **What's new at start-up.** The interactive CLI mentions a newer release, with the command that upgrades this install when it can tell how TradingAgents was installed, and notices from Tauric Research for the running version. It checks at most once a day in the background, so a run never waits on it; runs without a terminal never check, and `TRADINGAGENTS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` turns it off.
- **Release downloads.** Each GitHub release carries the source archive and a wheel, so a version installs with `pip install` from i

releases.name: TradingAgents v0.6.0
releases.body:
HTML reports, a provider per model tier, past decisions settled for every ticker while the analysts work, and company news read while Yahoo's news feed is down.

## Added

- **HTML report.** A saved report also includes `complete_report.html`, the report as one page with its sections listed beside the text, that reads well in a browser, on a phone and in print. Answering the save question at the prompt also asks about the page and can open it in your browser; `--no-html` or `save_reports(..., html=False)` skips it. The page is self-contained: it loads nothing and runs nothing. (#1419)
- **A provider per model tier.** The quick and deep models can run on different providers, for example the managers on Claude while the analysts run on OpenAI: set `deep_think_provider` or `quick_think_provider` (`TRADINGAGENTS_DEEP_THINK_PROVIDER`, `TRADINGAGENTS_QUICK_THINK_PROVIDER`) with the tier's model. The report header names each tier's provider. (#1440)
- **Past decisions settle alongside the analysts.** While a run's analysts work, every logged decision whose holding period has passed is settled, for any ticker, not only the one being analyzed. If settling fails, the run goes on and the repo

aiSummary.oneLiner: A robust research framework for developing, testing, and deploying autonomous AI agents for algorithmic financial tra...
aiSummary.whatItDoes: TradingAgents provides a comprehensive environment for building autonomous software agents capable of executing complex algorithmic trading strategies. The framework abstracts the intricacies of market data ingestion, strategy execution, and broker API integration. It allows developers to focus on designing agent logic—utilizing reinforcement learning, statistical models, or LLMs—while the system handles real-time data streaming, order management, and portfolio tracking. The project includes extensive backtesting capabilities to rigorously evaluate agent performance against historical market data before live deployment.
keyFeatures: Agent Logic Abstraction: Separates trading strategy implementation from the underlying mechanics of data handling and order execution.
Robust Backtesting Engine: Provides tools to simulate agent performance against extensive historical market data with realistic slippage and fee models.
Real-Time Data Ingestion: Connects to live market data feeds to provide agents with up-to-the-millisecond pricing information.
Broker API Integration: Handles the complex, secure communication required to route orders to live trading exchanges or brokerages.
Performance Analytics: Generates detailed reports and metrics to evaluate strategy effectiveness.

useCases.title: Algorithmic Strategy Development
useCases.description: Provides a structured environment for quantitative researchers to implement and test complex, automated trading models.

useCases.title: Reinforcement Learning Experimentation
useCases.description: Allows AI developers to train and evaluate reinforcement learning agents within simulated financial market environments.

useCases.title: Live Trading Automation
useCases.description: Facilitates the deployment of fully autonomous agents to execute trades in real-time markets without human intervention.

useCases.title: Strategy Backtesting and Validation
useCases.description: Enables rigorous historical testing of trading logic to ensure viability and manage risk before risking actual capital.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Quantitative analysts, algorithmic traders, and AI researchers focused on financial markets. It requires significant expertise in financial modeling, data analysis, and software engineering.
